mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Company Registration Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (or competent company registry of the jurisdiction of formation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document originates in an Apostille Convention state, obtain a Hague Apostille from that state's competent authority. If it originates in Taiwan, use consular legalization only: notarization by a Taiwan District Court notary, authentication by the Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in the destination jurisdiction. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (or other company registry of jurisdiction of incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan is not an Apostille state, so use only the consular legalization path: request a recent official certificate, notarize it at a Taiwan District Court, certify at the Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize at the destination's Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (for Mainland China, use SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification). If the certificate is issued in an Apostille state, apply for a Hague Apostille instead; do not combine the two methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company board of directors / shareholders and legalized corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution must be notarized in the jurisdiction of execution. If that jurisdiction is an Apostille state, the notarized resolution should be apostilled directly. If executed in Taiwan, the resolution must follow consular legalization through the Taiwan notary/MOFA/representative office route. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, never sequential, authentication methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A certified copy of the Articles must be notarized by the origin jurisdiction's notary. For an Apostille state, issue a Hague Apostille from the competent authority. For Taiwan, use the consular legalization sequence: court notarization, MOFA authentication, and consular legalization at the destination's Taipei Economic and Cultural Office. Do not chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Corporate Creditworthiness
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic or international financial institution maintaining the JV's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by two authorized officers on bank letterhead. If the destination requires authentication, and the bank is in an Apostille state, the bank signature must be notarized and apostilled; if the bank is in Taiwan, use notarization and consular legalization. A bank may refuse notarization, in which case obtain the counterparty's written waiver. Never apply apostille after consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and every 25% or greater ultimate beneficial owner against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, Mainland China PBOC/SAFE designations, and Taiwan FSC AML/CF

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, notably Articles 1, 2, 6, 8, 129 to 156, 170 to 208, and 387, as supplemented by the Taiwan Foreign Investment Act and the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Articles 73 and 79, insofar as the mainland Chinese shareholder must obtain investment approval, together with the applicable financial supervisory rules administered by the Financial Supervisory Commission of Taiwan.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Central Company Registration Office, Taipei, Taiwan R.O.C.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act, accompanied by the certified Articles of Incorporation and the applicable investment approval certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No universal minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Taiwan Company Act for a Company Limited by Shares. However, all subscribed capital must be fully paid in cash by the shareholders before registration; the funds must be originated from each shareholder's external bank account and remitted to a temporary capital account in the Company's name. The funds are de facto blocked until the Ministry of Economic Affairs has granted the company registration and the certified public accountant capital verification report has been filed. No government escrow account is required; bank remittance records and a CPA certificate of capital verification serve as the regulatory evidence. For the factoring license, the Financial Supervisory Commission will separately assess prudential capital adequacy and may impose additional capital conditions before licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_JV_LTD, a Taiwan-incorporated Company Limited by Shares formed as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture under the Taiwan Company Act. The undersigned directors, holding a validly convened board meeting and having confirmed the presence of a quorum, hereby adopt the following resolutions. 1. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation in Taiwan, and that the Chairperson is authorized to execute the lease, building identification application, and all municipal occupancy filings, and to post the registered signboard at such address. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is confirmed as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, being divided into fully subscribed ordinary shares subscribed by the founding shareholders, together with any non-resident shareholders permitted by the investment approval; that the paid-in capital has been or shall be remitted in cash to the temporary bank account in the name of the Company from each subscriber's external account; and that the directors direct the establishment of a share register and subscription records showing each shareholder's number of shares and the amount paid prior to filing. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company opens and maintains corporate accounts at the designated bank, and that the Chairperson, General Manager, and Financial Controller, acting in any two-signature combination, are jointly authorized to open accounts, sign banking forms, execute SWIFT payment instructions, and issue escrow instructions for factoring and reverse-factoring settlement accounts. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed: Chairperson, General Manager, Company Secretary, Chief Financial Officer, and Anti-Money-Laundering Compliance Officer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting; the Company Secretary is directed to file the officers' names and specimen signatures with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the Financial Supervisory Commission. 5. AML AND GOVERNANCE POLICIES. RESOLVED, that the board adopts the draft internal control, customer due diligence, suspicious transaction report, sanctions screening, record-keeping, and FATCA/CRS compliance policies, and instructs the AML Compliance Officer to implement training, monitoring, and audit protocols before the commencement of factoring transactions. 6. REGISTRATION AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company Secretary is authorized to prepare, execute, notarize and submit the Company Registration Application, Articles of Incorporation, capital verification report, board resolutions, and all statutory attachments to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the National Taxation Bureau, and the Financial Supervisory Commission, and to pay all official fees, respond to official queries, and accept the Certificate of Incorporation. All resolutions are immediately effective and may be relied upon by all third parties. PASSED unanimously by the board on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Commission Authorization and Sino-Foreign Joint Venture Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan R.O.C.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for approval of an inward investment from the parent organizations and, if applicable, the mainland Chinese joint-venture shareholder, covering the proposed Taiwan Company and its factoring business scope. The Commission will review the legality of the source of funds, national security implications, shareholding ratio, and sector eligibility. Include a project feasibility report, capital plan, signed joint venture agreement, and draft Articles of Incorporation. All shareholder signatures must be notarized and, if executed abroad, legalized by the competent authority in the jurisdiction of execution or otherwise authenticated for use in Taiwan. The approval certificate is a prerequisite for every later company registration and financial license application. Respond fully to any Commission request for economic concentration or ownership transparency information.
required_dossiers: Joint venture agreement and draft Articles of Incorporation
Audited financial statements or bank references of each shareholder
Business plan for accounts receivable factoring and cross-border reverse factoring
Certificates of incorporation and board resolutions of all parent entities
Power of attorney for the local agent
Identity documents and registry excerpts of each shareholder
Source-of-funds declaration and bank reference letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit supplemental source-of-funds and ownership-chain evidence; if suspended, apply for leave to cure within the prescribed period; if the investment is rejected, restructure the shareholder or business scope and file a fresh application after correcting the grounds of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Name and Business Scope Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Company Name Reservation Application online using the reserved Chinese and English names and the exact proposed business scope of factoring, cross-border reverse factoring, and trade-supply-chain finance. The system will examine the name against existing registrations and administrative regulations, and the business scope will be checked against permitted activities for a company limited by shares. The resulting name reservation certificate is valid for six months. It must be included in the incorporation filing under the same applicant identification used in the Investment Commission approval.
required_dossiers: Proposed business scope in English and Chinese
Applicant identification or unified business number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusion or identical similarity, propose alternate names and refile; if the business scope is rejected as overly broad, narrow the wording and resubmit; if the system requires revision, obtain a formal rejection note and use it to correct the filing before the reservation expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution, Bank Account Opening, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-licensed commercial bank chosen by the Company and a Taiwan-certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital account in the Company's name at a Taiwan bank before registration. Each subscriber must transfer the subscribed paid-in capital from its external bank account by wire, with the remitter name stated and the purpose marked as capital contribution. After funds are received, the bank issues a capital confirmation proof. Engage an independent Taiwan CPA to review the remittance instructions, bank statements, foreign exchange settlement records, subscriber identities, and the draft Articles. The CPA will issue a capital verification report stating that the capital has been actually paid. The funds remain in the temporary account and may not be withdrawn until the company registration certificate is issued; this provides an effective blocked-capital condition.
required_dossiers: Bank account application and specimen signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the wire, submit source-of-funds affidavits and MT103 payment confirmations; if the CPA declines verification due to a missing reference, request the remitting bank to issue a corrected purpose code and re-confirm; if the transfer is returned, repeat the transfer after updating the remittance reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Central Company Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Central Company Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application to the Central Company Registration Office. Attach the certified Articles of Incorporation, the first board resolution, the CPA capital verification report, bank capital proof, investment approval certificate, name reservation certificate, lease agreement with landlord written consent, and identification or registry documents of directors and shareholders. Pay the filing fee and retain the receipt. The Ministry will verify corporate capacity, paid-in capital, legal objective, registered office situs, and statutory officers. Upon approval, the Ministry issues the Company Registration Certificate and transfers the basic data to the National Taxation Bureau for unified business number issuance. The company legally comes into existence on the effective date recorded on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Identification and registry documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice is issued, file the supplemental documents within the requested period; if registration is denied, obtain written reasons, correct the defects, and refile; if a curable formality is identified, the registry may allow correction within fifteen days without restarting the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Financial Supervisory Commission Factoring License Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance and the Financial Supervisory Commission, R.O.C., Banking Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, apply to the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration, uniform invoice registration, and employer registration; obtain the tax registration certificate and tax identification number. Concurrently submit to the Financial Supervisory Commission a formal application for approval to operate as a factoring and reverse-factoring institution. The application must demonstrate paid-in capital, compliance governance, AML/CFT controls, customer due diligence systems, information security, and a sufficient compliance officer. The FSC will examine the fitness of shareholders, directors, and senior management. The company may not execute factoring transactions until the FSC license is granted. After approval, maintain the license as a condition of continuing operation.
required_dossiers: Tax registration application and director identification
FSC application for factoring institution approval
Board-approved internal control and AML/CFT policy
AML/CFT compliance officer appointment and resume
Operational and information technology system manual
Financial risk management and sanctions screening policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC inquires about KYC or source-of-funds issues, submit enhanced declarations and independent audits; if the license is denied on prudential grounds, adjust the compliance structure or capital base and resubmit; if tax registration is delayed, remedy the missing unified number by resubmitting the tax registration form and director identification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, R.O.C., Banking Bureau, and Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factoring and Reverse-Factoring Business Institutional License (FSC Approval and Company Registration with Financial-Services Business Scope)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan R.O.C.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the Company is a pure financial services institution under ISIC 6492 with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. No Environmental Impact Assessment report, self-registration, or pollution control permit is required for the registered office. If the registered office operation is limited to administrative data processing and transaction settlement, no environmental licensing applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, volatile organic compounds, chemical emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated. The Company must nevertheless manage office waste in accordance with the Waste Disposal Act, including recycling of electronic equipment, paper, batteries, and rejected payment-card or token hardware; any future physical fulfillment center would require a separate environmental registration under the EPA categories.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The Company must obtain the fire safety inspection or fire safety equipment certificate for the commercial office premises before occupancy, as required under the Fire Services Act and the Regulations on the Installation and Maintenance of Fire Safety Equipment. The local fire department will verify fire alarms, escape routes, emergency lighting, and extinguishers. For a low-risk financial office, no industrial fire permit or high-hazard structure clearance is required; however, the legal building certificate and the landlord safety documents must be retained in the corporate register. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the employer must complete the mandatory workplace self-inspection for office ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency evacuation, and maintain records of designated labor health and safety staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Tax Administration of Taiwan, acting through the relevant Regional National Taxation Bureau; the supporting online electronic portal is the Ministry of Finance electronic taxation service portal, supplemented by the E-Invoice Consolidation Service platform for indirect tax filings and invoice transmission.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident equity joint venture must first complete the statutory incorporation or investment approval process administered by the competent authority for foreign investment, then file a tax registration application with the Regional National Taxation Bureau before commencing business. The Bureau issues a tax registration certificate that records the statutory Uniform Invoice Number, which is the eight-digit enterprise tax identification number used for VAT/business tax, income tax withholding, and customs declarations. For a non-resident enterprise without a fixed place of business but providing cross-border services or digital services into Taiwan, the enterprise must apply for a Ministry of Finance-assigned Tax Identification Number directly through the electronic tax portal, register for business tax on qualifying electronic services, and file periodic VAT/business tax returns through the designated online channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not maintain a check-the-box election or an elective hybrid-mismatch classification. A limited joint-venture company is treated as a taxable entity at the entity level under the Income Tax Act, subject to the ordinary corporate income tax regime; financing and factoring arrangements remain subject to arm's-length pricing and thin-capitalisation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act (Taiwan VAT/Business Tax system)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary threshold exempts an enterprise from the obligation to file tax registration; every enterprise selling taxable goods or services in Taiwan must register before commencing business. Full VAT-taxable status requiring Uniform Invoice issuance is mandatory once average monthly taxable sales reach NT$200,000; smaller traders below that threshold may be taxed at the 1% small-scale enterprise rate and may be exempt from Uniform Invoice issuance until the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan does not operate a real-time customs-style VAT clearance with digital stamping. Instead, the statutory system is the Uniform Invoice system. VAT-registered enterprises must issue electronic Uniform Invoices through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Consolidation Service, transmit invoice records in the prescribed electronic format through the statutory Turnkey interface, and upload e-invoice data within the legally prescribed filing cycle. Anti-fraud integrity is achieved through centrally controlled invoice numbering, batch transmission, cross-matching of sales and purchase invoices, and audit controls exercised by the National Taxation Bureau.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act for goods physically exported from Taiwan, for services rendered in Taiwan that are directly connected with and necessary for the export of goods, and for qualifying services supplied to non-resident recipients and consumed outside Taiwan. For cross-border supply-chain factoring, the relevant service fees can be zero-rated only if the underlying receivable is genuinely attributable to an export transaction, the service is performed for a non-resident counterparty, and the documentary evidence demonstrates that the service is not consumed in Taiwan. Domestic or onshore factoring services remain taxable at 5% unless the statutory export-service conditions are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) issued by the Customs Administration evidencing physical export from Taiwan
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing shipment from Taiwan to the foreign buyer or end customer
Bank Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a trade-settlement currency
Underlying sales or service contract identifying the non-resident counterparty
Evidence connecting the cross-border factoring or trade-finance service to the qualifying export transaction
Proof of repatriation of foreign exchange proceeds through authorised financial channels
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the taxpayer cannot produce the prescribed export documentation or the foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period, the National Taxation Bureau will reverse the zero rating, reassess VAT at 5% on the gross consideration, and impose overdue interest and late-payment penalties. Where zero-rating is supported by forged export declarations, artificial offshore arrangements, circular fund flows, or otherwise fraudulent documentation, the matter is treated as tax evasion under the Business Tax Act and the Tax Collection Act. The competent tax authority may retroactively claw back the tax concession, levy fines proportionate to the evaded tax at the statutory penalty multiples, and refer the case for criminal prosecution.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.note: This dossier applies to the Taiwan jurisdiction and uses the statutory Taiwan tax identity and indirect tax regime for the CN_JV_LTD cross-border factoring entity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The jurisdiction is the People's Republic of China (mainland China), not Taiwan, as the composite key indicates country_iso CN and jurisdiction_id TW, but the sovereign_country is China. Given the explicit 'sovereign_country' field with ISO CN, the applicable foreign exchange regime is the PRC's managed floating exchange rate system administered by SAFE under the PBC. Current account transactions are generally freely convertible subject to genuine trade and service background verification, requiring banks to perform 'three-in-one' checks (trade authenticity, customs data, and foreign exchange matching). Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment equity injections, shareholder loans, cross-border guarantees, and factoring-related cross-border receivables purchases, require stringent approval or filing with SAFE and the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) for outbound investment if applicable. Profit remittance for foreign-invested enterprises is permitted after audited annual financial statements, tax clearance, and verification of prior capital injection via the foreign exchange capital settlement system. Surrender rules historically required mandatory conversion of export proceeds, but as of the current regime, enterprises may retain foreign currency in designated bank accounts up to a cap based on the prior year's current account receipts; any excess must be sold to banks. However, trade-in-services and current account payments are settled directly with supporting documents. For factoring transactions, cross-border assignment of accounts receivable from mainland exporters to a Taiwan-related factor (or vice versa) requires compliance with SAFE's regulations on cross-border receivable financing, including reporting via the ASOne system, and may require a special 'cross-border factoring business file number'. Nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only for qualified corporate clients with real trade background, while onshore RMB forwards and swaps are available through the interbank market. The renminbi is not fully convertible on the capital account, and any cross-border RMB settlement for factoring must obtain SAFE filing if it involves capital items. Overall, the regime mandates rigorous documentation, timing thresholds, and bank-level pre-approval, with no discretionary access to offshore fintech EMIs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE regulations, export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into the domestic foreign exchange settlement account within the statutory time limit of 180 days from the date of actual export receipt, or the date of customs declaration if earlier, but the enterprise may apply for extension under genuine circumstances. There is no blanket mandatory conversion ratio since 2012; however, enterprises are required to settle or retain proceeds subject to the 'foreign exchange settlement account cap' (an upper limit computed as the current account receipts over the past 12 months times a risk-weighted coefficient). Current account foreign currency receipts must be verified for authenticity via the trade monitoring system, and any retention beyond the cap must be converted into RMB. For factoing and supply chain transactions, the underlying trade must be traceable through commercial invoices, customs declarations (if goods move across the border), and transport documents. The surrender obligation is effectively mandatory only to the extent of the cap, but any conversion must be executed through a designated domestic Tier-1 bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FINANCIAL REALITY CHECK: Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise Business, Airwallex) are legally barred from rendering principal banking or domestic FX settlement services to mainland China-registered entities because they hold no banking license from the PBC or SAFE. Their viability rating is LOW and legally prohibited. Such EMIs cannot open remote RMB or foreign currency settlement accounts with Chinese enterprise legal names, cannot process capital injections, and cannot obtain the required SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate. They can only serve as limited auxiliary payment tools for certain inbound/outbound trade flows if they partner with a mainland-regulated bank as the underlying clearing institution, but the corporate treasury must maintain all primary accounts at a Chinese Tier-1 bank. Any use of unregulated EMIs would trigger immediate KYC red flags and may cause the cancellation of the factoring license. Therefore, the sole viable route is a fully licensed Tier-1 domestic commercial bank with a designated foreign exchange business branch.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and the designated legal representative of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture are required to appear physically in-branch for the initial account opening in mainland China, unless the bank accepts a notarized power of attorney with consular legalization (apostille not recognized for China as China is not a member of the Hague Apostille Convention) for an overseas director. But in practice, for medium-risk factoring entities, the majority of mainland-incorporated JV directors (especially the Chinese party representatives) must be physically present. The foreign shareholder's authorized director may complete the interview via a sanctioned video call only if the bank has a remote onboarding framework approved by PBC (rare and limited to pilot zones). However, to meet the AML underwriting requirement, the statutory legal representative (who must be resident in mainland China) is obligated to attend in-person. The compliance committee will also require the presence of the AML Compliance Officer and Financial Controller for a live audit interview. Therefore, the mandate is a firm physical presence at the bank's designated branch, typically the head office-level corporate banking center, with no pure remote consular proxy opening available except for non-signing roles. For foreign shareholders in Taiwan, due to cross-strait restrictions, the Taiwan corporate director must retain a local notarized proxy in mainland China, but that proxy must still appear at the branch with original credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-layer ownership structure with a Taiwan-registered parent or FIE shareholder engaging in trade supply chain financing, raising suspicion of cross-border structural money laundering or underground factoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full chain of ownership until ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs with >25% shareholding), certified organizational chart, audited financial statements of all parent entities for the last two years, board resolutions approving the establishment of the JV, and a detailed business description map showing the physical existence of the Taiwan parent and its operational track record. Include statutory declarations from all UBOs and source-of-wealth reports for each equity contributor with bank references from their home jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Factoring of existing accounts receivable may disguise invoice discounting or 'fake trade' financing, where invoices are generated without genuine supply of goods or services, violating SAFE's authenticity requirement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a sample set of three historical factoring transactions from the JV's pilot run, including fully traceable trade contracts, customs declarations (if goods cross borders), bills of lading, air waybills, or warehouse receipts, tax invoices verified via China's VAT system (special VAT invoices), proof of delivery, and payment flows from the debtors. Commit to an independent trade verification agent such as SGS or Eurofins for site inspections. Execute a Master Factoring Agreement with the bank that includes an audit clause, and provide monthly aging reports with real-time connectivity to the bank's trade finance platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High turnover of funds through a single holding company account with receipts from multiple unrelated counterparties, potentially indicating that the JV is acting as a clearing house for illicit funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a treasury policy document specifying that all funding flows must be clearly identified with purpose codes, maintain separate collection accounts for each client to avoid co-mingling, and provide a list of qualified debtor counterparties with their bank and business registration details. Implement a 'whitelist' of debtors pre-approved by the bank, and provide six months of bank statements from the parent entity showing predictable and economically sound transaction patterns. Further, provide transaction monitoring software (e.g., TMS or ERP audit logs) evidencing that every movement is tied to a specific underlying receivable, with automated reconciliation and exception reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The JV engages in both early factoring and cross-border reverse factoring, creating an exposure to trade-based money laundering (TBML) via over-invoicing or under-invoicing of goods between mainland China and Taiwan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sponsor an independent transfer pricing analysis and commodity rationalization study to confirm invoice values are at arm's length. Provide prior-year customs data comparison for the same HS codes across the industry to prove price reasonableness. Engage a Big Four auditor to issue a TBML risk assessment and implement a claw-back protocol for any transaction exceeding +-15% pricing deviation. Supply evidence of the underlying supply chain (full purchase orders, quality inspection certificates, and BL/AWB proof) and grant the bank real-time access to the digitized trade document repository via a limited API or a secure portal.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, inbound capital from the Taiwan shareholder into the mainland bank must be structured as foreign direct investment (FDI) equity injection or shareholder loan. If equity, the Taiwan entity opens an offshore remittance of USD or RMB to the JV's Capital Settlement Account (资本金账户) at a Tier-1 Chinese bank. The remittance SWIFT MT103 must include the Purpose Code (e.g., '121010' for foreign investment acting party funds) and the comment line must reference the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate (FDI certificate) number. Before wiring, the JV must complete the FDI QR code registration via the local Administration for Market Regulation and SAFE. The bank must separately receive the payment notice and match it to the registration. Funds in the capital settlement account cannot be transferred to another account for domestic use until the bank has verified the capital narrative and performed a 'willing settlement' (capable of conversion to RMB) according to SAFE rules. If the injection is via shareholder loan, it must comply with the proportional debt-to-equity ratio (not exceeding 2:1) and be registered with SAFE's cross-border financing macro-prudential regulation. The JV should also open a separate Net-Profit Account for future dividend remittance. For injection where the parent is in Taiwan, banks will additionally require a notarized certificate of incorporation and a cross-strait direct remittance approval if the Taiwanese side remits USD via Taoyuan airport bank. All inbound funds must first pass through the bank's pre-verification system, and the bank is required to report the transaction to SAFE within five working days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade supplies from China to Taiwan or other regions should be settled using SWIFT MT103 wires for standard open-account payment, or through commercial documentary letters of credit (L/C) for structured trade. Factoring disbursements to mainland suppliers (when the JV acts as factor) are domestic RMB remittances only, requiring the bank to debit the JV's RMB settlement account and credit the supplier's account with the invoice reference. For cross-border reverse factoring where a Taiwanese importer finances its mainland suppliers, the Taiwan importer's bank initiates an MT103 to the JV's account in China; on settlement the JV releases funds to local suppliers via instant clearing (CIPS or bank-account-to-bank-account intraday). For trade settlement in USD, the JV must designate a track that avoids the use of correspondent banks under OFAC sanctions; all USD wires must be cleared via New York if the banking counterparty has US access, but for Taiwan transactions a direct RMB route via CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) is preferred to bypass currency risk. The JV will use the bank's trade finance portal to submit export/import documents for authenticity. For documentary collections, the bank will handle the shipping documents and effect payment through SWIFT MT400/MT202. All outbound FX payments require supporting documentation (contract, invoice, customs declaration) and must be submitted to the bank before the payment date; the bank then verifies and sends the MT103 with the correct purpose code (e.g., '121030' for trade in goods). If the JV lessens its tail risk, it can also use bank payment obligation (BPO) through SWIFT. The bank will charge a per-transaction fee and the JV must maintain minimum balances for the clearing lines.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD forward contracts (up to 5 years) with a licensed Chinese commercial bank, requiring a signed ISDA/CSA or local derivatives agreement and margin collateral fully cash-backed or through bank guarantees. These forwards must be tied to genuine trade exposures from the factoring book and evidenced by underlying invoices.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for offshore USD/TWD or USD/RMB exposure only for qualified entities with approved cross-border trade background; the NDF is settled in RMB or USD net difference based on the fixing rate at the PBOC or Taipei Forex Inc., but only via the bank's offshore branch if the JV has an offshore account. Onshore mainland banks are constrained from executing NDFs for local enterprises; the JV must route NDFs through the Taiwan parent's treasury or a special offshore vehicle.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term shareholder loans converted into RMB or USD, limited to matched funding from the parent and approved by SAFE for capital account hedging. The swap's notional cannot exceed the underlying foreign-currency debt, and the cash flows must be settled on an actual-exchange basis (not differential) for the initial principal unless the bank obtains a special SAFE approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders Meeting resolution approving statutory financial statements, directors and supervisors reports, and auditor reappointment; resulting minute book entries and, if a registered event occurs, the related MOEA registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: on or before 30 June of the following year; any extension must be approved by the competent authority under Company Act Article 170
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered resolutions are ineffective against bona fide third parties; MOEA may order rectification and impose administrative fines on responsible persons; continued shareholder and management paralysis allowing six months of suspended operations triggers administrative strike-off or dissolution under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Annual Income Tax Return including annual accounting report and tax reconciliation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan, local tax administration office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar fiscal year, filing window is 1 May through 31 May of the following year; for an approved special fiscal year, filing is due within five months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing results in ex officio assessment by the tax authority, a delinquency surcharge of 15% on the assessed tax, monthly delinquent interest, and potential administrative follow-up; persistent non-filing combined with a six-month cessation of business is an administrative strike-off trigger under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements certified by an ROC licensed CPA and the related independent audit report, filed when statutory audit thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services; duplicate copy with the National Taxation Administration in the annual income tax filing package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year non-public company meeting audit thresholds, no later than 30 June or the approved MOEA extension; if submitted with the annual tax return, the return deadline of 31 May prevails
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, obtain CPA attestation, or file annual financial statements can subject the company and responsible persons to fines under the Business Entity Accounting Act and Company Act; false or misleading CPA-certified reports create civil and criminal liability for directors and the certifying CPA; continued non-filing for six months may support administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and 10% Shareholding Registry Update, including transfer notification and annual confirmation at the shareholders meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration and Beneficial Ownership Database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following any share transfer that creates or alters a 10%-or-more shareholding or any change in directors, supervisors, or senior managers; annual confirmation at the ordinary shareholders meeting must occur no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Willful or negligent failure to file, or the filing of false information, carries administrative fines from NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 per violation under Company Act Article 22-1; unregistered transfers cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties; repeated violations may be treated as evidence of operational non-continuity for MOEA strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Factoring Business Report and AML/CFT Compliance Submission for an FSC-licensed or FSC-supervised trade-finance and factoring entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Taiwan, Banking Bureau or applicable FSC business bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, by 30 April; AML/CFT customer due diligence refresh and internal testing must be completed and available for inspection by the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit a materially complete annual supervisory or financial return may trigger FSC corrective orders, suspension of authorized factoring activities, administrative fines under the banking and financial supervisory laws, and ultimate revocation of the factoring or financing license for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent CPA audit is compulsory if any of the following applies: (a) paid-in capital is NT$30 million or more; (b) annual turnover or operating revenue is NT$100 million or more; (c) total assets exceed NT$200 million; (d) workforce headcount exceeds 100 employees; (e) the entity is listed on TWSE or TPEx; or (f) the entity holds an FSC financial, factoring, or financing license or otherwise falls within the FSC-supervised financial services sector. Licensed trade and supply-chain factoring entities are always subject to mandatory annual audit irrespective of the general commercial thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS/TIFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission for public companies and FSC-supervised financial institutions; for non-public companies outside the FSC financial sector, the Business Entity Accounting Act, the Regulations on Business Entity Accounting Standards, and the Taiwan SME Financial Reporting Standards apply. Audited financial statements must be reconciled to the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial ownership register is maintained at the registered office in Taiwan. Company Act Article 22-1 requires identification of any shareholder with direct or indirect shareholding or voting power of 10% or more, and any transfer creating or varying that threshold must be reported to MOEA within 30 days. There is no separate repetitive annual UBO declaration form; instead, the register is confirmed at the annual ordinary shareholders meeting, and an FSC-licensed factoring entity must additionally refresh AML/CFT beneficial-ownership data annually and report material findings to the FSC. Failure to keep the register current is a regulatory delinquency and may lead to fines and strike-off action.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax) plus 5% retained-earnings surcharge on undistributed profits; Taiwan Income Tax Act Article 5 and Article 66-9
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate may benefit from (i) a 15% R&D expenditure tax credit under Article 12-1 of the Act for Industrial Innovation; (ii) five-year corporate income tax exemption for qualifying strategic industries under the Free Trade Zone or Economic Pilot Zone regimes; (iii) investment tax credits for automation, energy efficiency and professional training; (iv) no factoring-specific patent box, but cross-border reverse-factoring income may be partially sheltered by a treaty where applicable (none in force for mainland China shareholders)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15 – Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, filed via the Ministry of Finance Tax E-Filing System (https://tax.nat.gov.tw); non-resident withholding and cross-border transactions are annotated on attached Form 14 and the related-party schedule (Schedule B)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar year), with quarterly provisional tax prepayments; for an approved fiscal year-end other than December 31, the annual return is due within the fifth month after the fiscal year-end
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: May 1 through May 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end (i.e., last day of the fifth month); non-resident shareholders' dividend/royalty/interest withholding must be remitted within 10 days of payment per Income Tax Act Article 92

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue: total factoring fees, discount fees, service commissions on purchased receivables, and reverse-factoring income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Taiwan-source factoring revenue received from mainland Chinese clients; do not net bad debts or expected credit losses; revenue from a foreign factor allocated to Taiwan under the substance-over-form rule must be included; attach Schedule B of related-party transactions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold / service cost: credit insurance premiums, direct funding costs, third-party credit assessment and subcontractor collection fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany interest on funding must not be classified here; apply a TNMM benchmarking study if any service is procured from the mainland Chinese parent; retain arm's length pricing documentation contemporaneously
If gross margin on cross-border factoring is below the OECD interquartile range, expect a transfer-pricing adjustment; any positive adjustment increases Box 8 and Box 10

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses (excluding interest): payroll, director attendance fees, rent, professional and consulting fees, marketing, and general administration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to a non-resident mainland Chinese parent for management services are deductible only if the service is genuinely rendered, the withholding tax at 20% is made on the Taiwan-source fee, and a local file proves the charge is arm's length; otherwise disallowed

A sustained operating loss while the mainland China parent earns guaranteed returns through factoring discount adjustments triggers anti-avoidance recharacterisation under Article 43-1; the JV must prove business substance in Taiwan

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income: interest on working capital loans, foreign exchange gains, gains on sale of purchased receivables, and other residual income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest from loans to the mainland Chinese affiliate must be priced at the reference rate and capitalised on a fully documented loan agreement; below-market interest is imputed as taxable non-operating income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses: foreign exchange losses, loss on disposal of receivables, and legal damages
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only realised currency losses are deductible; unrealised losses are not allowed and must be reversed; any payment to the Chinese parent for waived or discounted receivables must meet the arm's length standard

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before tax: operating income plus non-operating income minus non-operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The JV is taxed at the entity level; no transparency to either the Chinese or Taiwanese shareholders; public accounting must be reconciled to tax accounting on the accompanying reconciliation worksheet

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for non-deductible expenses and tax-exempt revenues: add back fines, penalties, excess entertainment, and excess intercompany interest; subtract qualifying exempt dividends
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the mainland Chinese parent in excess of the 3:1 thin-capitalisation ratio is added back; any management fee paid to a Chinese affiliate without proper withholding and CIGA evidence is also added back
Compute the Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) base; a factoring company with large interest income is particularly exposed to the AMT at a 12% tax rate over the normal tax base; use the higher amount

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 20%: multiply Box 10 by 20%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends declared to the mainland Chinese shareholder are not deductible; they are an after-tax distribution subject to separate WHT at the time of payment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: R&D credits, investment credits, and foreign tax credit (if any)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is available for mainland Chinese withholding tax because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement is not in force; other double tax relief is limited to the Taiwan domestic credit mechanism under Article 3-5

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retained earnings surcharge: 5% on undistributed earnings (Article 66-9)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a dividend is declared to the mainland Chinese parent before the annual return is filed, the distributed amount is excluded from the surcharge base; the 21% dividend WHT applies to the gross distribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax statements for non-resident payments: attach Form 14 documenting dividends, interest, royalties and management fees paid to non-resident shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit 21% WHT on dividends to the mainland Chinese investor, 15% on interest to non-resident financial institutions, and 20% on royalties/technical fees; no treaty reduction is available because the 2015 Cross-Strait Tax Agreement is not yet in force; if any treaty-reduced amount was used without a valid Tax Residency Certificate, the full statutory WHT plus penalties must be paid

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge: 1% of the unpaid tax for every two days of delinquency, up to a maximum of 15%; if no tax is due, a fixed penalty of NT$ 1,500 applies. Understatement or misstatement of income: civil penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax (Income Tax Act Article 110); willful tax evasion is subject to imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to NT$ 6 million under the Tax Collection Act Article 41. Failure to remit withholding tax on non-resident payments: a penalty of three times the unremitted amount and interest. Fraudulent cross-border invoicing or sham factoring transactions may additionally trigger money-laundering penalties of up to NT$ 10 million and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on gross dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder (effective from 1 January 2018), including a mainland Chinese shareholder; no reduced rate is currently available under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement because that agreement is not in force
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding rate under a Taiwan double taxation treaty, the non-resident shareholder must, before or at the time of the payment, file Form 15 Application for Tax Treaty Withholding Relief with the National Taxation Bureau, submitting (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the resident jurisdiction; (ii) a Beneficial Ownership Declaration; (iii) evidence of the shareholding period and percentage (treaty rates of 5% or 10% on dividends generally require a 25% or more shareholding held for at least 365 days); (iv) current audited financial statements and proof of Core Income-Generating Activities in Taiwan, and (v) an undertaking to notify the tax authority of any change in circumstances. The taxation bureau will issue a treaty relief certificate within 30 days; the payer may withhold at the treaty rate only after that certificate is obtained. Because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement signed in 2015 is not in effect, mainland Chinese shareholders cannot use the TRC protocol; statutory 21% WHT must be withheld and remitted within 10 days of payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on cross-border interest paid to a non-resident enterprise is 15%; statutory WHT on royalties and technical service fees is 20%. Under Taiwan's effective double tax treaties, interest is commonly reduced to 10% and royalties to 10% (exemption may apply to certain copyrighted software royalties). The same Form 15 and Beneficial Ownership protocol applies; a mainland Chinese lender or licensor remains subject to statutory 15% / 20% rates absent an effective DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$ 50 million of cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory preparation of a Taiwan Local File; NT$ 200 million of total related-party transactions triggers a contemporaneous transfer-pricing report and summary disclosure; Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting are mandatory when the group's consolidated revenue exceeds NT$ 27 billion, with cross-border related-party transactions over NT$ 20 billion
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 12-6 of the Tax Collection Act and anti-avoidance measures in Article 43-1 and Articles 43-3/43-4 of the Income Tax Act. For a factoring entity, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are: (i) credit underwriting and receivables due diligence; (ii) execution of the factoring or reverse-factoring contract; (iii) cash collection, ledger monitoring and default management; and (iv) management of the credit risk. CIGA must be performed in Taiwan by local staff with genuine decision-making authority. A Sino-Taiwanese JV acting as a mere booking centre for a mainland Chinese parent will be treated as not having economic substance, and the National Taxation Bureau may reattribute all Taiwan-source income to the actual management place, reject intercompany deductions, or impose a deemed assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion and Understatement of Factoring Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV deliberately fails to record factoring fees earned from mainland Chinese clients, receives collections into private director accounts, issues no unified invoice, and uses an HK/BVI intermediary to conceal more than NT$ 5 million of Taiwan-source income while credit and collection staff actually operate in Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, a civil penalty of up to three times the understated tax is imposed. Under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act, willful tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to NT$ 6 million; the National Taxation Bureau may also levy monthly delinquency surcharges and impose compulsory demand for unpaid taxes and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fraudulent invoicing or movable fund diversion are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid taxes, interest and penalties under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act. The corporate veil is pierced and personal bank accounts and real estate may be frozen/seized; individual directors are blacklisted by the National Taxation Bureau and prohibited from leaving the territory until taxes are settled, and may be sentenced to imprisonment for up to five years for criminal tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Cross-Strait Profit Shifting / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV has no physical office, no local staff, no board meetings in Taiwan, and merely passes 90% of its factoring margin to the mainland China parent as 'technology service fees' or 'guarantee fees' while all credit decisions, risk management and collection functions are performed in mainland China; the Taiwan entity is a paper shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Taxation Bureau invokes Article 43-1 and Article 43-4 of the Income Tax Act to disregard the Taiwanese JV, attribute the whole profit to the actual place of management (mainland China), and impose a reassessment plus interest. Article 12-6 of the Tax Collection Act denies any tax advantage from a sham arrangement. Civil penalty for the underpayment may be up to 100% to 300% of the corrected tax, and a resolution to dissolve the entity may be issued by the MOEA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the alter-ego doctrine, courts will pierce the corporate veil under Company Act Articles 154 and 367 and render the directors personally liable for the JV's tax debts. The tax authority may levy on directors' personal assets, obtain a court order for entity disregards, blacklist directors from serving on any board for three years, ban them from international travel, and prosecute them for criminal tax fraud, resulting in imprisonment of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV engages in cross-border reverse factoring for shell trading companies linked to the mainland Chinese parent, fails to obtain the statutory factoring license required by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, omits Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and suspicious-transaction reporting under the Money Laundering Control Act, and deliberately splits payments into sub-threshold SWIFT wires to evade AML surveillance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 15 and 16 of the Money Laundering Control Act, the conduct is punishable by imprisonment for six months to five years and a fine of up to NT$ 10 million. Unlicensed factoring violates Article 18 of the Financial Regulation and Development Act, attracting an administrative fine of NT$ 2 million to NT$ 20 million and revocation of the company registration; the Central Bank may also fine the company for unapproved cross-border payment settlement transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The limited-liability shield is removed for directors who knowingly conceal money laundering or conduct unlicensed financial business. Personal assets, including bank accounts and real property, are subject to criminal forfeiture; directors are blacklisted from serving as directors or officers of financial-capital type companies for life, barred from government procurement and foreign-exchange privileges, and may be denied exit from Taiwan. Criminal custodial penalties reach up to five years, with additional fines equal to the portion of laundered assets attributable to the director's acts.
